artists.biography:
Bad Brains is a hardcore punk band formed in Washington, D.C., in 1977. They are widely regarded as among the pioneers of hardcore punk, though the band's members objected to this term to describe their music. They are also an adept reggae band, while later recordings featured elements of other genres like funk, heavy metal, hip-hop and soul. Bad Brains are followers of the Rastafari movement.

Originally formed as a jazz fusion ensemble under the name Mind Power, Bad Brains developed a very fast and intense punk rock sound which came to be labeled "hardcore", and was often played faster and more emphatically than the music of many of their peers. The unique factor of the band's music was the fact that they played more complex rhythms than that of other hardcore punk bands, also adapting non-punk style guitar riffs and solos into their songs.

Bad Brains have released nine studio albums (one of which is entirely composed of instrumental versions of their past material). The band broke up and reformed several times over the years, sometimes with different singers or drummers. Since 1998, the lineup of singer H.R. (Human Rights), guitarist Dr. Know, bassist Darryl Jenifer, and drummer Earl Hudson has reunited, albeit performing sporadically.

perplexity.description:
I Against I" is the third studio album by American rock band Bad Brains, originally released in 1986 on SST Records. The album marks a pivotal moment in the band's discography, expanding beyond their hardcore punk roots to incorporate elements of funk, soul, reggae, and heavy metal. This stylistic diversity is evident throughout the record, with tracks ranging from blistering hardcore anthems to melodic reggae-infused songs, showcasing the band's musical virtuosity and genre-blurring approach. The album's title track, "I Against I," is particularly notable for its philosophical lyrics and dynamic shifts in tempo and mood.

Commercially, "I Against I" became the best-selling album in Bad Brains' catalog, solidifying their influence within the punk and alternative rock scenes. Critics have praised the album for its innovation and energy, highlighting its role in inspiring a generation of bands across multiple genres. It is widely regarded as one of the most important rock albums of the 1980s and has been included in influential lists such as "1001 Albums You Must Hear Before You Die." The album's blend of aggression, melody, and genre experimentation cemented Bad Brains' reputation as pioneers of hardcore and alternative rock.
